Google Meet attendance tracker for online tutors & bootcamps

Private tutoring, test-prep academies (SAT/IELTS/GRE), coding bootcamps, and language schools rely on accurate student hour logs for billing, parent communication, and course completion certificates. Here is how to automate attendance tracking in Google Meet.
Attendance Tracker for Tutors
Student hours and duration report exported to Google Sheets

Eliminate Billing Disputes: When parents ask why they are being billed for a missed lesson or late arrival, you have an uneditable, timestamped Google Sheet record showing exact join and leave times down to the minute.
Why Tutors & Bootcamps Need Dedicated Tracking
Proof of Billable Hours: If you bill $60/hour, every 15 minutes of unrecorded student time or disputed attendance costs you real money.
Late Arrival Tracking: Know immediately if a student joined 10 minutes late (+10m late) so you can adjust the lesson pacing.
Disconnections & Reconnects: When a student has spotty Wi-Fi and rejoins three times, Attendance Tracker calculates their total cumulative time in call.
Multi-Session Course Tracking: For 8-week bootcamps or semester packages, view total hours logged across all sessions with automated streak tracking.
How It Works for Online Tutors
Step 1: Start Your Google Meet Lesson
Launch your 1-on-1 or small group tutoring session from Google Calendar or Google Classroom. Open Attendance Tracker from the Activities panel in Google Meet.
Step 2: Real-Time Roster & Punctuality Flags
The side panel tracks student arrival timestamps. If your scheduled lesson starts at 4:00 PM and the student connects at 4:12 PM, the panel automatically flags them as +12m late.
Step 3: One-Click Google Drive Sync

When the session concludes, Attendance Tracker creates a tabbed spreadsheet in your Google Drive named Meet Attendance Tracker. You can share read-only links with parents or paste the hours directly into QuickBooks, Wave, or your invoicing software.
